risks.risk: Primary account is currently passed as the Core actor instead of the validated POS employee.
risks.impact: Incorrect attribution and replay actor substitution.
risks.mitigation: Extend acquisition/execution context and move employee attribution inside the atomic result.

risks.risk: No trusted Offline device or event-governed employee authority exists.
risks.impact: Sensitive cache or commands could be unlocked by browser state alone.
risks.mitigation: Server registration, one-device unique constraint, device proof, signed allowlists, generations and trusted-reconnect revocation discovery.

risks.risk: Production authority differs from repository assumptions.
risks.impact: SQL or runtime work may target absent/drifted authority.
risks.mitigation: Approved read-only Production attestation completed; inherit exact findings and require separate correction design.

risks.risk: Post-Core employee/inventory/audit/WhatsApp behavior is outside one idempotent transaction.
risks.impact: Duplicate or missing effects on retry.
risks.mitigation: Atomic attribution/mutation and unique server effect ledger.

risks.risk: Core supports four of eight required payment representations.
risks.impact: Offline replay contract cannot preserve current product semantics.
risks.mitigation: Extend canonical validation/receipt contract before pilot.

risks.risk: No inventory snapshot version or inclusion frontier.
risks.impact: Double deduction or overselling after refresh.
risks.mitigation: Consistent branch snapshot and receipt frontier.

risks.risk: Mode A cannot resist a compromised browser/device.
risks.impact: Plaintext is available while unlocked and keys are usable by compromised origin/device.
risks.mitigation: Managed device, least data, CSP/supply-chain controls, explicit human acceptance; optional future Mode B hardening.

risks.risk: One-device branch uniqueness may contend during replacement.
risks.impact: Two active authorities or branch lockout.
risks.mitigation: Partial unique index plus transactional replacement and audit.

risks.risk: Browser/device key loss makes local ciphertext unrecoverable.
risks.impact: Loss of unsynced work.
risks.mitigation: Explicit recovery policy, server receipts retained, online-only fallback; do not fake recovery.

risks.risk: Official numbers generated offline could collide.
risks.impact: Accounting duplication.
risks.mitigation: Local temporary references only; server transaction issues official numbers.

risks.risk: Long offline backlog creates lock/latency spikes.
risks.impact: Deadlocks, timeouts, poor recovery.
risks.mitigation: Receipt-first bounded batches, deterministic stock locks, backoff, stop on dependency conflict.

risks.risk: Conflict auto-resolution changes paid totals or quantities.
risks.impact: Financial/customer mismatch.
risks.mitigation: No silent rewrite; employee/manager resolution through new commands.

risks.risk: Stale feature switches cannot convey a remote kill decision during outage.
risks.impact: Locally authorized work may continue until trusted reconnect.
risks.mitigation: Server enforces every acquisition/effect; authorized local administrative lock applies immediately; UI warns remote changes may be unknown.

risks.risk: Inactive provisioning SQL may still differ from runtime authority until independently reviewed and qualified.
risks.impact: Authority/ACL/RLS regression if executed prematurely.
risks.mitigation: Keep all SQL review-only, use exact whole-file waves, manifest/static tests, independent review, and a separately authorized isolated qualification before any execution.

risks.risk: Current application PIN verification and actor-session issuance are Online-only, while employee presentation is sessionStorage-only.
risks.impact: No supported Offline employee selection exists in the active application after restart.
risks.mitigation: Use verified Online account bootstrap plus a separate structured local employee selector; never infer actor from Primary Auth or presentation state.

risks.risk: A four-digit employee selector PIN has only 10000 values.
risks.impact: A copied selector verifier can be brute-forced and must never be treated as protection for business-data encryption.
risks.mitigation: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 600000 iterations, unique 32-byte salt, bounded local attempts and managed device controls; keep device-bound encryption independent of PIN.

risks.risk: Browser-local attempt counters and clocks can be modified by a privileged attacker.
risks.impact: Lockout/delay or audit ordering may be bypassed outside the supported application.
risks.mitigation: Authenticated sequence/hash-chained state and fail closed on counter deletion/rollback; clock and sync age never control authority lifetime; acknowledge no tamper-proof Mode A guarantee.

risks.risk: Remote employee/device/permission/PIN-generation/branch revocation is unknowable during a complete outage.
risks.impact: Revoked authority may continue indefinitely on the disconnected device.
risks.mitigation: Trusted reconnect validation before synchronization/acquisition, authorized local administrative lock, exact purge/quarantine, immutable command attribution and an explicit UI warning.

risks.risk: Server PIN hash, plaintext PIN, unsalted SHA-256, or reversible credential is reused as an Offline selector.
risks.impact: Credential disclosure and incorrect account/data authority.
risks.mitigation: Use only the separately enrolled structured PBKDF2 selector verifier; keep it outside Auth and the device encryption hierarchy.

risks.risk: Copied browser profile contains ciphertext and potentially usable non-extractable key handles depending on platform.
risks.impact: Offline credential attack moves beyond the intended physical device boundary.
risks.mitigation: Disable profile roaming/backup, bind generations, managed OS account, full-disk encryption, with Mode B available as optional hardening.

risks.risk: Clearing origin storage resets attempt state.
risks.impact: Attacker retries or operator loses protected offline data.
risks.mitigation: Credential/key/counter co-dependency; missing state locks and requires online reactivation; no local unlocked bootstrap.

risks.risk: Not every authorized branch employee is pre-enrolled before outage or the 25-employee pilot cap is exceeded.
risks.impact: Product requirement is only partially met during outage.
risks.mitigation: Enrollment roster monitoring, pre-shift enrollment, explicit cap approval and Online enrollment for new employees; age alone never removes an enrolled employee.

risks.risk: A queued command is rebound to the employee active during replay.
risks.impact: False audit attribution and unauthorized execution.
risks.mitigation: Immutable bootstrap/account/employee enrollment IDs and generations in command AAD and Core acquisition; mismatch is terminal quarantine.

risks.risk: Mode B capabilities are claimed without per-platform proof.
risks.impact: Software-backed key, backup, screen, or attempt behavior may be weaker than policy assumes.
risks.mitigation: Capability/attestation matrix per OS/device; unsupported platforms fail closed and use online-only mode.

risks.risk: Historical repository schema text includes a plaintext-display PIN field and is misused as Offline authority.
risks.impact: PIN disclosure and immediate 10000-value credential compromise.
risks.mitigation: Offline package rejects plaintext PIN/server verifier inputs; do not infer Production state; require a separate security/SQL decision for any actual plaintext storage.

risks.risk: Local PIN selection expands permissions or rewrites account, scope, device, namespace, or authority generations.
risks.impact: Client-created authority could bypass trusted issuance.
risks.mitigation: PIN may only select one exact enrolled employee; exact order.create allowlist and immutable account/device/bootstrap/employee bindings fail closed.

risks.risk: PIN is allowed to restore Offline access after explicit establishment logout.
risks.impact: Logout fails to terminate usable account authority.
risks.mitigation: Explicit logout disables Offline PIN entry and retains commands encrypted/inaccessible; only same-account Online reauthentication can recover.

risks.risk: Phase 5 or durable outbox bypasses the account/bootstrap/employee authority chain.
risks.impact: Commands can be created without verified account and real employee/device attribution.
risks.mitigation: Mandatory graph: Online account → device → device encryption → employee selection → bootstrap → outbox → Core bridge → pilot; all flags remain false.
